> Author: researcher (vfx-deep-research workflow) · claude-sonnet-5-5 · default effort · 2026-10-12

# P1 Elements: GAMEPLAY and SHAPE

Scope: Part 1 of the VFX-designer evidence base. Field framework: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition (Keyser / Riot LoL style guide). Timing words: windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

Method notes (read these first)
- Every source id below was opened with WebFetch (or, for the Roblox spec, read from the local mirror). Search snippets were NOT cited as proof.
- The most important primary source, the 2017 Riot LoL VFX style guide PDF, could NOT be read (see section 5 and 6). All of its content here comes through later Riot posts (S01-S04) or the VFX Apprentice relay (S05, tier C). Claims that rest only on S05 carry "needs 2nd source".
- Web search budget ran out mid-run. Not searched: Arcane/Fortiche, Spider-Verse/Imageworks, Insomniac, Santa Monica, Embark, Epic first-hand. Follow-up search needed (section 5).
- Fetch-tool summaries were small-model summaries of pages, so quotes are "as returned by the fetch tool". Re-verify a quote against the page before using it in an owner-facing document.

## 2. Findings

Element table. Column meanings: "effect on feeling" and "effect on energy" are what the element does to the viewer; "n/a" = the source says nothing on that axis. "Energy" = how loud/forceful/urgent the effect reads. No number is invented: "no number found" means exactly that.

### 2.3 Roblox capability facts (spec only, not design evidence)

| design need | Roblox feature | fact | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| directional streak / slash | ParticleEmitter.Orientation | FacingCamera (default), FacingCameraWorldUp, VelocityParallel (aligned with movement), VelocityPerpendicular | S26 spec |
| vertical elements, floor rings | Orientation / FacingCameraWorldUp | stays upright on world Y while facing camera | S26 spec |
| scale pop, stretch | ParticleEmitter.Size (NumberSequence) + Squash | squash curve over lifetime, >0 narrower/taller, <0 wider/shorter | S26 spec |
| flipbook breakup | FlipbookLayout, FlipbookFramerate, FlipbookMode | Grid2x2 (4), Grid4x4 (16), Grid8x8 (64), Custom; framerate max 30 fps; OneShot divides Lifetime evenly by frame count | S26 spec |
| dissipation | Transparency NumberSequence, Lifetime | fade at start and end avoids pop-in/out; lifetime cap 20 s | S26 spec |
| cost | Rate, Size | up to 400 particles per second per emitter (100 on mobile); larger particles cost more fill-rate; low-memory clients turn flipbooks off | S26 spec |
| motion trail | Trail | lifetime in seconds sets trail length (doc sample 0.5 vs 3.0); FaceCamera keeps it visible from every angle | S26 spec |

## 4. Conflicts between sources (newer first, what changed)

| topic | sources | what disagrees | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Value range for effects [V: confirmed S05 wording 'avoid using the extremes of 0 or 100 and lean towards using more of the mid-range' (2022-08-29, author not named on page); page does NOT mention pure white for ultimates] | S05 (guide relay: avoid 0% and 100%, build mostly from mid values) vs S03 (area of focus uses highest and lowest value = highest contrast) | one says avoid extremes, the other says focus takes the extremes | INFERENCE: palette stays mid-range, extremes reserved for the focus tier. Unverified because the 2017 guide is unread (snippets said pure white is saved for ultimates; NOT read). |
| Where "readability" ranks | S03 (2020: communicating gameplay while minimising noise is objective 1) vs S01 (2022: readability is "secondary", after fixing gameplay accuracy such as hitbox indicators) | wording differs | Consistent when read together: truthful gameplay information first, readability second, theme third. Newer (S01) is more precise. |
| Indicator honesty | S01/S04 (indicator equals real hit area; over-promising is a defect) vs S20 (player indicator slightly smaller, enemy slightly larger than hitbox) | S20 teaches a deliberate lie | S20 is tier C-, uncredited; tier A wins. Treat S20 as an owner-decision option, not a rule. |
| Angular shapes mean threat | S18 (2007, angular V captures attention as threat) vs S19 (2015, angularity is disliked; threat does not fully explain it; curved shapes approached faster) | threat vs preference | Newer (S19) says preference and threat are both involved. No 2020+ replication found. Using "sharp = threat" for VFX is inference. |
| Edge softness | S05 (mix soft and hard) vs S08/S21 (hard-edged masks) vs S12 (hard geometric smoke) | different games, different styles | Not a real conflict: edge hardness follows how truthful the edge must be and how stylised the game is. |
| Effect length | S05/S06 (keep short) vs S04 (big-gameplay spells may be noisier) | length vs amount of noise | Not a conflict. Length and noise both scale with importance. |
